papers.title: Acupotomy for Cervical Spondylosis-Related Neck Pain: A Study Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.authors: Li X, Yang W, Lv Z, Zhang J, Tang M, Wang L et al.
papers.abstract:
Cervical spondylosis (CS) is a common source of neck pain and imposes a substantial global health burden. Conservative treatments, including oral medication, physical therapy, and rehabilitation exercises, are widely used in clinical practice, but their effects are often limited or slow to become apparent. Acupotomy, a minimally invasive intervention that combines acupuncture principles with soft-tissue release techniques, may alleviate CS-related neck pain by releasing local adhesions and reducing muscle tension. However, methodologically rigorous evidence from randomized controlled trials regarding its efficacy and safety remains limited.
This study is a prospective, assessor- and statistician-blinded, randomized parallel-group trial involving patients with CS-related neck pain. The primary hypothesis is that an ultrasound-guided acupotomy-based treatment strategy is more effective than standard medication in reducing pain intensity in patients with CS-related neck pain. Eligible participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either an acupotomy group or a control group. To strengthen methodological rigor and minimize potential assessment bias, the trial incorporates assessor and statistician blinding, standardized ultrasound guidance during the acupotomy procedure to improve precision and safety, and a predefined sample size calculated based on statistical power analysis. The intervention consists of a 3-week treatment period, followed by a 12-week follow-up period after completion of treatment. The primary outcome will be pain intensity assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS). Secondary outcomes will include the Neck Disability Index (NDI), cervical range of motion (ROM), and health-related quality of life as measured by the 36-item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36). The primary efficacy analysis will be performed using the full analysis set, defined as a modified intention-to-treat population.
This trial is designed to evaluate the comparative effectiveness and safety of an ultrasound-guided acupotomy-based treatment strategy compared with celecoxib for CS-related neck pain. The findings of this study are expected to provide clinically relevant information regarding the feasibility, safety, and potential clinical value of this treatment strategy.
International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry (ITMCTR2026000837). Registered on 31 March 2026. The protocol was approved by the Ethics Committee of the First Affiliated Hospital of Shandong First Medical University on 11 March 2026 (YXLL-KY-2026(062)).

papers.title: Patients Experience of Ear Acupuncture for Anxiety-A Qualitative Interview Study.
papers.authors: Berggren A, Stjernkvist R, Hedberg L, Larsson C, Rusch K, Aiff H
papers.abstract:
This study aimed to qualitatively explore and understand the experiences of patients with anxiety undergoing National Acupuncture Detoxification Association (NADA) treatment in a psychiatric outpatient setting.
Through interviews, 20 participants shared their experiences after receiving 10 NADA treatments. The data were meticulously analyzed using latent content analysis to identify recurring themes and patterns.
Four themes emerged from the analysis: "A gradually increasing sense of well-being," "Relief that lasted temporarily or throughout the treatment period," "A feeling of inner peace and relaxation," and "A transient feeling of discomfort and disappointment," reflecting ambivalence regarding the tangible benefits of the treatment.
The findings reveal a multifaceted landscape of experiences with NADA treatment for anxiety. While the majority experienced relief and anticipatory sentiments, it was evident that the benefits were not universally experienced. The study underscores the need for continued research and optimization of the NADA protocol to cater to diverse patient needs within psychiatric outpatient settings.
NADA treatment could pose a nonpharmacological option for some patients with anxiety. Patients experienced anxiety relief, and many wanted to continue treatment.
Patients/users of outpatient psychiatric care participated in the study as participants. They were then interviewed to share their experience.

papers.title: Beyond the barrier: Engineering the tumor-immune-soil nexus-a mechanistic blueprint for integrating Traditional Chinese Medicine with immunotherapy in metastatic colorectal cancer.
papers.authors: Sun Y, Li Y, Jiang H, Liu X, Yu S, Liu Y
papers.abstract: Metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) presents a stark immuno-oncologic dichotomy: while microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) tumors respond to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), the vast majority of microsatellite-stable (MSS) cases remain refractory, underscoring a critical need for novel strategies to convert "cold" tumors into "hot" ones. This review advances the hypothesis that Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) can serve as a formula-defined ecological conditioner within the tumor-immune-soil nexus. We propose a mechanistic blueprint where TCM formulas, rather than acting as nonspecific immunostimulants, function as multi-target systems that re-engineer the tumor microenvironment. The framework integrates three actionable pillars: (1) remodeling the gut microbiome to restore immune-competent consortia and metabolic flux, (2) reprogramming the myeloid compartment away from suppressive M2 macrophages and MDSCs toward immunostimulatory states, and (3) inducing immunogenic cell death to generate critical danger signals. By translating classical concepts like the Gan Pi axis into modern immunometabolism, we propose that TCM can prime the "soil" to sensitize MSS mCRC to ICI therapy. However, realizing this potential requires a paradigm shift from descriptive reports to rigorous, biomarker-driven trials. A crucial point is that the nature of a significant portion of existing human evidence remains observational, cross-sectional, or case-control; this limits causal inference and hinders the reconstruction of the long-term temporal sequence extending from the reciprocal dynamics of the immune system and microbiome to cancer progression or treatment response. We conclude that the future of TCM-ICI integration lies in standardized, chemically characterized formulas evaluated within adaptive platform trials, utilizing spatial transcriptomics and microbiome-humanized models to validate true cold-to-hot conversion.

papers.title: Use of complementary and alternative medicine and its association with antiretroviral therapy adherence and quality of life among people living with HIV in urban Indonesia: a cross-sectional study.
papers.authors: Juliawaty A, Ashan D, Zakiyah N, Fitria N, Nainu F, Bahar MA
papers.abstract: HIV remains a major global health concern, and complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) is often used alongside antiretroviral therapy (ART). This cross-sectional study assessed CAM use, associated factors, perceptions, and relationships with ART adherence and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) among people living with HIV (PLHIV) in Indonesia. From June to September 2025, 400 PLHIV attending three primary healthcare centers in Makassar completed standardized interviewer-administered questionnaires. Overall, 158 (39.5%) reported current CAM use, predominantly herbal remedies. In exploratory bivariate analyses, CAM use was associated with older age, comorbidity, family support, self-reported mode of HIV acquisition, and hospitalization history (all p < 0.05). CAM users more frequently perceived CAM as safer than conventional treatment (65.2% vs. 40.9%). ART-adherence categories differed between groups (p = 0.006), although high adherence was comparable (87.3% vs. 88.8%). CAM use was associated with a lower EQ-5D-5L utility index in the unadjusted analysis (B = -0.039; 95% CI: -0.065 to -0.013), but not after adjustment (B = -0.020; 95% CI: -0.046 to 0.006). CAM use was not associated with EQ-VAS scores. CAM use was common but was not independently associated with poorer HRQoL. Routine CAM screening and individualized counseling may help identify potential CAM-ART interactions and support safe HIV care.

papers.title: Reproducibility of Published Meta-Analyses on Acupuncture for Irritable Bowel Syndrome.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Zou K, Liu D, Guo Q, Deng Y, Long Y
papers.abstract:
Published meta-analytic results should be reproducible from information available to readers. We assessed the numerical reproducibility of pairwise meta-analytic estimates of acupuncture for irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
We searched six English- and Chinese-language databases. Eligible systematic reviews reported at least one direct pairwise meta-analysis with recoverable study-level inputs. Each eligible pooled estimate was recomputed. The primary outcome was result-level numerical reproducibility. A prespecified standardized reanalysis was a key secondary analysis. Proportions used review-clustered robust variance estimation.
Twenty-three systematic reviews contributed 176 pooled estimates. Of these, 144 (81.8%, 95% confidence interval [CI] 71.4%-92.2%) reproduced exactly, 21 (11.9%, 95% CI 4.2%-19.7%) approximately, and 11 (6.3%, 95% CI 1.4%-11.1%) showed substantive numerical discrepancies. All 11 exceeded the 5% threshold for CI width, whereas 10 retained point estimates within 5% of the published value. No original-method recomputation changed whether the 95% CI excluded the null value. I2 reproduced within one percentage point for 162 estimates (92.0%). The text and forest plot disagreed on the analytic model for 12 of 168 evaluable estimates (7.1%). Under the standardized framework, 26 of 174 estimable results (14.9%; 95% CI 7.5%-22.3%) changed from statistically significant to nonsignificant.
Published pooled estimates were generally reproducible when study-level inputs were recoverable, although uncertainty estimates were more sensitive than point estimates. Complete, internally consistent reporting and availability of data and code would facilitate independent verification.

papers.title: Mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation: a new perspective on metabolic regulation in respiratory diseases.
papers.authors: Wei S
papers.abstract: Chronic respiratory diseases pose a major global public health challenge, and the role of metabolic reprogramming in their pathogenesis has attracted increasing attention. Mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation (FAO) is a core energy metabolic pathway that not only fuels pulmonary tissues but also participates in essential physiological processes such as alveolar surfactant synthesis. This review outlines the molecular mechanisms of mitochondrial FAO and focuses on its complex regulatory roles in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, asthma, pulmonary fibrosis, acute lung injury/acute respiratory distress syndrome, lung cancer, and pulmonary arterial hypertension. We further summarize potential FAO-targeted therapeutic strategies, including small-molecule drugs, exercise and nutritional interventions, and active components of traditional Chinese medicine, based largely on preclinical evidence from animal models and in vitro studies. These findings provide a theoretical framework for future clinical research, though the direct clinical translatability remains to be validated.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture alleviates spinal cord injury by regulating M2-like polarization of myeloid cells through CMPK2/NLRP3 inflammasome inhibition.
papers.authors: Zhang K, Zhang M, Chen Y, Ni Z, Huang Y, Ying X et al.
papers.abstract: This study aims to investigate the roles of CMPK2 and the NLRP3 inflammasome in the phenotypic polarization of myeloid cells after spinal cord injury (SCI), as well as the underlying regulatory mechanism of electroacupuncture (EA). Wild type (WT) and CMPK2 knockout (CMPK2 KO) mice were subjected to SCI induction, followed by NLRP3 overexpression or EA intervention. Motor function, inflammatory responses, and CD11b + myeloid cell phenotypes were evaluated. SCI induced severe motor dysfunction, excessive neuroinflammation, and upregulated the expression of CMPK2, NLRP3, and IL-1β. Neuronal NLRP3 overexpression exacerbated pro-inflammatory M1-like polarization of CD11b + myeloid cells and aggravated tissue damage. CMPK2 KO inhibited NLRP3 inflammasome activation, suppressed pro-inflammatory M1-like polarization, and promoted anti-inflammatory M2-like polarization of myeloid cells. EA intervention exerted similar neuroprotective effects by inhibiting the CMPK2/NLRP3 signaling axis and promoting the shift of CD11b + myeloid cells toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype. These findings indicate that activation of the CMPK2/NLRP3 axis is closely associated with excessive neuroinflammation and imbalanced phenotypic polarization of myeloid cells after SCI. EA can ameliorate SCI-induced neurological damage by targeting the CMPK2/NLRP3 axis to mitigate neuroinflammation and promote reparative phenotypic polarization of myeloid cells. This study provides novel insights into potential anti-inflammatory strategies for SCI.

summary.question: 전침이 척수손상 후 CMPK2/NLRP3 경로와 골수계 세포의 M1/M2 유사 분화에 어떤 영향을 주는지 평가했다.
summary.methods: 척수손상 마우스에서 WT와 CMPK2 결손 모델, NLRP3 과발현, 전침 중재를 비교하며 운동기능, 염증반응, CD11b+ 골수계 세포 표현형을 분석했다.
summary.results: 척수손상은 CMPK2, NLRP3, IL-1β를 증가시켰고, 전침은 CMPK2/NLRP3 축을 억제해 염증성 M1 유사 분화를 줄이고 항염증성 M2 유사 분화를 촉진하며 신경학적 손상을 완화했다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 전침은 척수손상 관련 염증 조절의 잠재적 전략으로 해석될 수 있으나, 본 결과는 동물실험이므로 임상 적용 전 추가 근거가 필요하다.
summary.limitations: 동물모델 연구로서 사람 척수손상에 대한 직접적 근거는 아니며, 전침의 임상효과를 단정하기 어렵다.

pico.c: 대조군, CMPK2 결손 또는 NLRP3 과발현 조건
pico.o: 운동기능, 신경염증, CD11b+ 골수계 세포의 M1/M2 유사 분화
